The 4 without are exactly the claimed list, and the 14 with are exactly the dateline list of item 4 - one partition, no residue, no verse in neither class. The rule holds, the list is right, and it is complete.

items.my_list: CONFIRMED 5 of 6: 45:17 ובחדשים, 46:3 ובחדשים, 47:12 לחדשיו, 18:31 לב חדש, 36:26 לב חדש. REFUTED 1 of 6: Ezek.11.19.
items.note: REFUTATION: MT 11:19 does NOT read לב חדש. Its bytes read לֵב אֶחָד ('one heart') and its only חדש-root token is חֲדָשָׁה, which modifies רוּחַ - 'a NEW SPIRIT', not a new heart. I confirmed there is no ketiv at 11:19 that could supply חדש: every one of its 16 tokens is pointed, and this extract marks ketiv by leaving a token unpointed (as at 47:12 והיו). A full root sweep of the book confirms 11:19 is the only one of the three that lacks a bare חדש token: 18:31 and 36:26 each carry BOTH לב חדש and רוח חדשה; 11:19 carries only רוח חדשה. The likely cause is the well-known text-critical variant (many MSS and the versions read חדש for אחד at 11:19, which is why many English versions print 'a new heart' there) - but WLC/OSHB, the declared source of truth, reads אֶחָד, and this campaign quotes Hebrew strings as byte claims. IMPORTANT - the RULE is unaffected: 11:19 is still correctly excluded, and for the right reason, since חדשה is an adjective and not the date construction לחדש/בחדש. Only the illustrative gloss misnames what 11:19 reads. OTHER חדש FORMS - I swept every חדש-root token in the book (28 distinct verses, 8 distinct token forms) and found four families the exclusion note does not name, all correctly excluded and none date-like in the numbered sense: החדש 'the new moon' at 46:1 and 46:6 (וביום החדש, a recurring cultic occasion with NO day number, the same class as ובחדשים); חדשים 'months' at 39:12 and 39:14 (seven months, duration); the bare absolute חדש inside the 32:1 dateline (already captured there via לחדש); and חדשה at 11:19. I also checked for alternate month vocabulary: ירח occurs in only 2 verses, 32:7 (the moon as a celestial body) and 43:9 (וירחקו, root רחק, not a month at all), so no date formula escapes through a synonym. Verdict: no verse is wrongly included and no verse is wrongly excluded - the rule's behavior is fully correct - but one named example reading is false, and the exclusion list is incomplete by the 46:1/46:6 החדש family.

Skeleton of 45:18: כה אמר אדני יהוה בראשון באחד לחדש תקח פר בן בקר תמים וחטאת את המקדש. The messenger formula כה אמר אדני יהוה is present and stands verse-initially; my independent messenger sweep returns 122 verses, exactly matching the inventory list element-for-element, and Ezek.45.18 is in it. The month+day formula בראשון באחד לחדש is present as a contiguous token run, matching the toolkit's quoted string exactly. Both halves confirmed, and the combination is genuine: 45:18 is the only one of the four calendar dates that opens with the messenger formula, so the toolkit's 'watch this one above all' is well-founded.

The Hebrew היה stands as a free-standing quoted lexeme delimited by spaces, not spliced inside an English word; the earlier 'the הest perfect form' defect is gone. unresolved_uncertainty.what: The 11:19 error is duplicated in BOTH shipped artifacts - ezek_device_inventory.json line 631 (calendar_dates_not_datelines.correction_2026_09_08) and TOOLKIT.md line 187 - so a repair must touch both or the two will disagree.
unresolved_uncertainty.why_it_matters: A downstream writer trusting the gloss could quote לב חדש as MT 11:19's bytes in a row citation, shipping a fabricated quotation into the graph. That is the exact error class the byte-fidelity discipline exists to prevent, and it is the same class as the 13-vs-14 and 3-vs-4 misses this repair round was opened to fix.

unresolved_uncertainty.what: A naive re-implementation of vayehi_any that allows an UNBOUNDED infix returns 47, not 41, because it swallows the six dateline verses whose structure is 'vayehi [date] hayah dbr yhwh 'ly' (26:1, 29:17, 30:20, 31:1, 32:1, 32:17). I hit this myself on my first pass and had to constrain the infix to exclude the perfect verb היה.
unresolved_uncertainty.why_it_matters: The 41 figure is correct, but the inventory gloss says only 'allowing an INFIXED temporal phrase' without stating that the infix must not be the perfect verb. That underspecification silently blends the vayehi family into the hayah family - precisely the never-blend error the three-way split exists to prevent - and it will bite the next agent who rebuilds the sweep. Worth tightening the gloss even though no count is wrong.

e19_selfreport: ran no listing, no glob, no recursive search; read only the exact paths named
overall_rationale: Four of the five delta items confirm outright, and item 2's RULE behavior is fully correct - the four-verse list, the 14-verse dateline complement, the 39/41/7 counts, the puncta, the 45:18 double formula, and the cleaned note all re-derive exactly from the source bytes. The single blocker is narrow and fixable in one token: the newly-authored correction sentence asserts that MT 11:19 reads לב חדש, and it does not - it reads לב אחד with רוח חדשה. Because that false byte claim sits inside the repair text itself and is duplicated in both artifacts, accepting it would ship a fabricated Hebrew reading inside a correction note whose whole purpose is byte fidelity. Recommended minimal cure: in ezek_device_inventory.json line 631 and TOOLKIT.md line 187, drop 11:19 from the לב חדש example (leaving 18:31/36:26, both verified) or restate 11:19 as רוח חדשה 'a new spirit'; optionally add the 46:1/46:6 החדש family to the exclusion list and tighten the vayehi_any gloss. No count, list, or rule changes.
